items.ex: Un caffè e un cornetto, per favore.
items.ex_en: A coffee and a croissant, please.
items.notes: Often ed before a word starting with e: lui ed Elena. Don't confuse with è (is).
Goes right before the verb, and before object pronouns: non lo so.

items.ex: Il caffè e la pizza sono buoni.
items.ex_en: The coffee and the pizza are good.
items.notes: il: most masculine nouns. lo: masculine before s+consonant, z, gn, ps (lo zaino). l': before a vowel (l'amico, l'acqua). la: feminine.
i = plural of il (i treni); gli = plural of lo and masculine l' (gli zaini, gli amici); le = feminine plural (le case).

items.ex: Un caffè e una birra, per favore.
items.ex_en: A coffee and a beer, please.
items.notes: uno before s+consonant or z (uno zaino); un' before a feminine vowel (un'amica); masculine has no apostrophe (un amico).
Subject pronouns are usually dropped: Sono americano. Use them for emphasis or contrast.
For friends, family, kids and peers. With strangers use Lei.
Takes third-person verb forms: Lei parla inglese? Often capitalized in polite writing.

items.ex: Lei è la mia amica Giulia.

items.notes: Plural 'you'; also used to address a group politely.

items.ex: Il ragazzo che parla è mio fratello.
items.ex_en: The guy who's talking is my brother.
items.notes: Also joins clauses: So che è tardi = I know (that) it's late. Never dropped like English 'that'. In exclamations: Che bello! = How nice!
che cosa, cosa and che all mean 'what?'. Cos'è? = What is it?
dov'è = where is.
Also 'when' in statements: Quando piove, resto a casa.
The answer also uses perché (= because). Written with an acute accent: é.

items.ex_en: I'm staying here because I'm tired.

items.notes: Also 'like/as': come te = like you. Com'è? = What's it like?
Agrees with the noun: quanto, quanta, quanti, quante (Quanti anni hai?). Quanto costa? = How much is it?
Before è it becomes qual è — no apostrophe! Plural quali.
Anch'io = me too.
Very common conversation starter. Can also mean 'at that time'.

items.ex_en: It's raining, so I'm staying home.

items.ex: Prima il museo, poi il pranzo.

items.ex_en: First we eat, then we go.
items.notes: prima di + noun or infinitive = before: prima di cena, prima di partire.
dopo + noun = after: dopo cena.

items.ex_en: If you want, we'll go together.
items.notes: No accent. Sé (with accent) means 'oneself'.
di + article = del, dello, della, dell', dei, degli, delle. Also 'some': del pane. Origin: sono di Boston.
a + article = al, allo, alla, all', ai, agli, alle. Cities take a (a Milano); ad before a word starting with a (ad Assisi).

items.en: from; at/to someone's place; since, for (time)
items.notes: da + article = dal, dallo, dalla, dall', dai, dagli, dalle. Vado da Marco = I'm going to Marco's. Studio italiano da due mesi = I've been studying Italian for two months.

items.ex_en: I'm going to Italy in May.
items.notes: in + article = nel, nello, nella, nell', nei, negli, nelle. Countries: in Italia; transport: in treno, in macchina.
Usually not combined with the article: con il, con la (col exists but is less common).
per + infinitive = in order to: per imparare. Not combined with the article.

items.ex_en: The phone is on the table.
items.notes: su + article = sul, sullo, sulla, sull', sui, sugli, sulle.

items.ex_en: I'll be there in ten minutes.
items.notes: Interchangeable; choose by sound (fra tre, tra fratelli). Between: tra Roma e Firenze.

items.ex: Un caffè senza zucchero, per favore.

items.notes: Also reflexive: mi chiamo… = my name is… (literally 'I call myself').

items.ex: Ci porta il conto, per favore?
items.ex_en: Could you bring us the check, please?
items.notes: Ci vediamo! = See you! (literally 'we'll see each other').

items.ex_en: This one? Yes, I'll take it.
items.notes: Becomes l' before a vowel or h: l'ho visto.

items.ex_en: The key? I can't find it.
items.notes: Capitalized La = you (formal object): La ringrazio = thank you (formal).

items.ex_en: Is there a café near here?
items.notes: Singular. Plural: ci sono. Non c'è = there isn't / he's not here.

items.ex_en: There are a lot of tourists today.

items.ex: Questo è il mio amico Marco.
items.notes: Forms: questo, questa, questi, queste.
Before a noun it changes like the article: quel ragazzo, quello zaino, quell'albergo, quei ragazzi, quegli zaini; feminine quella, quelle.
Forms: il mio, la mia, i miei, le mie. Usually with the article, but none with a singular family member: mia madre.
Forms: tuo, tua, tuoi, tue.
Agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: la sua macchina = his/her car. Forms: suo, sua, suoi, sue.
Forms: nostro, nostra, nostri, nostre.
Before a noun add the article: tutto il giorno, tutta la notte, tutti i giorni.
Needs non before the verb (double negative). On its own: Niente! = Nothing!

items.ex_en: Do you want something to drink?
items.notes: qualcosa di + adjective: qualcosa di buono = something good.
Invariable; always followed by a singular noun: ogni giorno.

items.ex: Non bevo mai il caffè la sera.
items.ex_en: I never drink coffee in the evening.
items.notes: Double negative: non + verb + mai.
Non c'è più = there's none left / it's gone.

items.ex: Io prendo il pesce, tu invece?
items.ex_en: I'll have the fish — what about you?
items.notes: invece di = instead of: invece del vino, l'acqua.

items.ex_en: Shall we take the train or the bus?

items.notes: Stressed forms used after prepositions: con te, per me, da me, a te.

items.ex: Arrivo dopo, cioè verso le nove.
items.ex_en: I'll come later, I mean around nine.
items.notes: Also a very common filler: Cioè… = I mean… / Like…

items.ex: È caro, però è molto buono.
items.ex_en: It's expensive, but it's very good.
items.notes: Similar to ma, slightly more emphatic.

items.ex_en: I read while I wait for the train.

items.ex: Sembra buono, e infatti è ottimo.
items.ex_en: It looks good, and sure enough, it's excellent.
items.notes: Confirms what was just said. It does NOT introduce a contradiction (for 'actually' use in realtà).

items.ex_en: I don't even have one euro.
items.notes: Neanch'io / Nemmeno io = me neither.

items.ex_en: Maybe tomorrow we'll go to the beach.
items.notes: Magari! on its own = I wish! / If only!
Also 'in short / basically', or impatient 'come on!'.

items.ex_en: There are like a hundred people.
items.notes: Informal, like English filler 'like'. As a noun: il tipo = type, kind; guy.
In everyday speech gli also means 'to them'. Also the plural article (gli amici).
Le (formal) = to you: Le porto il menù. Also 'them' (feminine direct object) and the plural article.
Replaces a place already mentioned: a Roma? — Sì, ci vado.

items.ex: Quante ne vuole? — Ne vorrei due.
items.ex_en: How many would you like? — I'd like two.
items.notes: Replaces a quantity of something already mentioned; often has no English equivalent.
Needs non before the verb. As an adjective it changes like un: nessun problema, nessuna idea.

items.ex_en: I'm staying here a few days.
items.notes: Invariable and always followed by a SINGULAR noun, even though it means 'a few': qualche giorno.
Plural only; feminine alcune.
Forms: vostro, vostra, vostri, vostre.
Invariable, always with the article: il loro, la loro, i loro, le loro.

items.ex: Non è caro, anzi, è economico.
items.ex_en: It's not expensive — actually, it's cheap.
So, let's see… I'll have the pasta.
May I sit down? — Of course!
items.notes: Also: certamente, come no!

items.ex: Dov'è la fermata? — Non lo so, mi dispiace.
items.ex_en: Where's the stop? — I don't know, sorry.
items.notes: Also just: non so.

items.en: here it is; there you go; that's it
items.notes: Ah, ecco! = Oh, I see! / That's it! Eccomi! = Here I am!

items.ex: Ci sono tante cose da vedere, per esempio il Colosseo.
items.ex_en: There's lots to see, for example the Colosseum.

items.notes: Also encouragement. Ma dai! = No way! / Really?
Used alone to agree strongly.

items.ex_en: Excuse me, how much is it?
items.notes: senti = informal, senta = formal. Used to get attention or to introduce a point.

items.ex_en: It's closed? Oh well, we'll come back tomorrow.
items.notes: Short for va bene; also spelled va be'. Informal.
Very informal; avoid in formal situations.
